questions.question: Which of the following best defines a Horn clause and provides a correct example?

options.A: A clause that contains at most one positive literal, e.g., ¬P ∨ ¬Q ∨ R
options.B: A clause that contains exactly two positive literals, e.g., P ∨ Q ∨ ¬R
options.C: A clause that contains only negative literals, e.g., ¬P ∨ ¬Q
options.D: A clause that must be a biconditional, e.g., (P ⇒ Q) ∧ (Q ⇒ P)

questions.explanation:
A Horn clause is “a disjunction of literals containing at most one positive literal” (page 180). Option A matches this definition and gives a valid example; the other options violate the definition.

---

questions.question: Convert the propositional formula (A ⇒ (B ∧ C)) ∧ ¬D into an equivalent formula in Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF).
questions.explanation:
Implication is rewritten: A ⇒ (B ∧ C) ≡ ¬A ∨ (B ∧ C). Distribute ∨ over ∧ to obtain (¬A ∨ B) ∧ (¬A ∨ C). Adding ¬D gives the CNF (¬A ∨ B) ∧ (¬A ∨ C) ∧ ¬D, which is option A (see definitions of literal, clause, CNF on page 180).

---

questions.question: Which inference rule is complete for propositional logic when the knowledge base is expressed in CNF?
questions.explanation:
The text states that the “Resolution rule: rule: complete for propositional logic in CNF” (page 180). Hence resolution is the complete rule; the other rules are not guaranteed to be complete for arbitrary CNF KBs.

questions.question: Transform the first‑order logic sentence ∀x (P(x) ⇒ ∃y Q(x,y)) into an equivalent clause set in CNF (after Skolemization). Which of the following is the correct result?
questions.explanation:
Steps: eliminate ⇒ (¬P(x) ∨ ∃y Q(x,y)), move ∃ outward, Skolemize y to f(x), and drop quantifiers → clause ¬P(x) ∨ Q(x, f(x)) (page 203 provides a similar example of converting quantified sentences to CNF). Option A matches this clause.

questions.question: Given the knowledge base KB = {A ∨ B, ¬A}, does KB entail B? (Use the definition KB |= α iff KB ∧ ¬α is unsatisfiable.)

options.C: It cannot be determined without additional information.
options.D: Both A and B are true in different models.

questions.explanation: To test entailment, add ¬B to KB: {A ∨ B, ¬A, ¬B}. The clauses force A to be true (from A ∨ B together with ¬B) but also require ¬A, which is contradictory; thus the set is unsatisfiable, so KB |= B (page 180). Hence option A is correct.
